A digital health informatician specializing in business analysis who authors L2 DAK components. Business analysts translate clinical guidelines and normative products into structured DAK artifacts including business processes, data dictionaries, decision-support logic, and requirements.
Key activities: - Review L1 source documents and extract structured content - Author generic personas based on task-shifting guidelines - Create user scenario narratives - Design BPMN 2.0 business process diagrams - Define core data elements and data dictionary - Develop decision-support logic tables (DMN standard) - Develop scheduling logic tables - Define indicators and performance metrics - Capture functional and non-functional requirements - Streamline content across DAK components for consistency
**Source**: IG Starter Kit, L2 DAK Authoring, Section 2.1 "Fill in DAK components"; Community of Practice page

Logical Model for representing Generic Business Processes and Workflows from a DAK. A business process is a set of related activities or tasks performed together to achieve the objectives of the health programme area.

CodeSystem for the Classification of Digital Health Services and Application Types v2, as defined in the Classification of Digital Interventions, Services and Applications in Health (CDISAH), second edition (2023). ISBN 978-92-4-008194-9.
Services and Application Types represent the types of software, ICT systems and services or communication channels that deliver or execute digital health interventions (DHIs) and health content.

A clinician or subject matter expert (SME) of a specific health area who validates the clinical accuracy and completeness of DAK content against WHO guidelines and other normative products. SMEs should be the authors of the source documents or recognized experts actively engaged in, if not leading, the collaborative development of the DAKs.
Key activities: - Validate that DAK components accurately reflect L1 recommendations - Provide clinical ground-truthing through country visits and interviews - Identify gaps or needed changes in DAK content - Review decision-support logic for clinical correctness - Confirm that workflows represent 80% of clinical scenarios - Validate personas against real-world practice settings - Advise on cross-programme overlaps (e.g. TB/HIV indicators)
**Source**: IG Starter Kit, L2 DAK Authoring, Sections 1 "Plan" and 2.2 "Validate"

A frontline member of the health workforce who delivers health interventions at the community level, acting as a link between communities and formal health facilities. Community health workers are a key sub-group of healthcare providers.
Community health workers use DHIs to: - Register and follow-up community members (2.1, 2.2.1) - Receive community-based decision support and job aids (2.3) - Report public health events from point of diagnosis (3.3.1) - Access mobile training and competency assessments (2.8) - Communicate with supervising clinical staff (2.5.1) - Manage their daily visit planning and activities (2.7)
**ISCO-08**: 3255 (Community health workers), 5321 (Health care assistants).
**Examples**: Village health worker, health extension worker, community health volunteer, lay health advisor, peer educator, traditional birth attendant, community case manager.

A designated reviewer responsible for approving SMART Guidelines content at key decision gates in the authoring lifecycle. Content Reviewers ensure that DAK and IG content meets quality standards, accurately reflects WHO normative guidance, and is ready to proceed to the next phase.
Content Reviewers may be senior technical officers, programme leads, or designated governance committee members. They provide formal sign-off at phase transitions (L2→L3, draft→publication).
Key activities: - Review and approve L2 DAK content before L3 authoring begins - Review and approve L3 IG content before publication - Assess whether content changes are breaking or non-breaking - Approve draft publications for stakeholder circulation - Provide final sign-off for release publication - Ensure content aligns with WHO guidelines governance policies - Participate in cross-programme content harmonization reviews
**Source**: IG Starter Kit, Publication page (review process); DAK Authoring, Section 2.2 "Validate DAK content with SMEs"

Logical Model for representing Core Data Elements from a DAK. A core data element can be one of: a ValueSet, a CodeSystem, a ConceptMap, or a Logical Model adherent to SGLogicalModel. This is the ONE EXCEPTION to allowing FHIR R4 models into the DAK LMs.

An L3 author who creates machine-readable FHIR artifacts from L2 DAK specifications. FHIR Modellers use FSH (FHIR Shorthand), SUSHI, and the IG Publisher toolchain to produce conformant Implementation Guides.
Key activities: - Verify L2 input availability and consistency - Author FHIR Logical Models from L2 data dictionaries - Create FHIR Profiles (StructureDefinitions) - Author FHIR Questionnaires from L2 forms - Write CQL for decision logic, scheduling logic, and indicators - Create StructureMaps for data extraction - Author PlanDefinitions for business processes and decision tables - Create ActorDefinitions from L2 personas (reusing Commons repository) - Create ExampleScenario resources from L2 user scenarios - Author FHIR Measure resources from L2 indicators - Create FHIR Requirements resources - Develop test cases (TestPlan, TestScript, example instances) - Ensure all artifacts conform to CRMI Shareable/Publishable profiles
**Source**: IG Starter Kit, L2-L3 Overview and all L3 authoring pages

Base logical model providing the common schema metadata interface inherited by all SMART Guidelines logical models. Every SMART Guidelines logical model schema derives from this base, which documents the shared FHIR and JSON-LD metadata properties used by the JSON Schema generation pipeline.
Logical Model for representing Functional and Non-Functional Requirements from a DAK. A high-level list of core functions and capabilities that the system must have to meet the end users' needs.
Logical Model for representing functional requirement from a DAK

Logical Model for representing Generic Personas from a DAK. Depiction of the human and system actors. Human actors are end users, supervisors and related stakeholders who would be interacting with the digital system or involved in the clinical care, public health or health system pathway.

Source reference for Generic Persona - exactly one of the following must be provided: - url (url data type): URL to retrieve GenericPersona definition from input/ or external source - canonical (canonical data type): Canonical URI pointing to the GenericPersona definition - instance: Inline GenericPersona instance data

A professional who manages, analyses, and disseminates health data to support evidence-based decision-making. This corresponds to the 'Data services' user group in CDISAH v2, providing crosscutting functionality across the health system.
Data managers use DHIs to: - Create data collection forms and manage data acquisition (4.1.1) - Store and aggregate health data (4.1.2) - Synthesise and visualise data for reporting and dashboards (4.1.3) - Apply automated analytics and predictive modelling including AI/ML (4.1.4) - Parse, de-duplicate, and curate coded datasets and terminologies (4.2) - Classify disease codes and causes of mortality (4.2.3) - Map geographic locations of facilities, events, populations, and providers (4.3) - Enable point-to-point data integration and standards-compliant interoperability (4.4) - Maintain data governance including authentication, privacy, and consent (4.5)
**ISCO-08**: 2120 (Mathematicians, actuaries and statisticians), 2521 (Database designers and administrators), 2523 (Computer network professionals), 3120 (Computer network and systems technicians).
**Examples**: Biostatistician, epidemiologist, health informatician, data analyst, DHIS2 administrator, GIS specialist, interoperability engineer, terminology manager.
Logical Model for representing Health Interventions and Recommendations from a DAK. Overview of the health interventions and WHO, regional or national recommendations included within the DAK.

Source reference for Health Interventions - exactly one of the following must be provided: - url (url data type): URL to retrieve HealthInterventions definition from input/ or external source - canonical (canonical data type): Canonical URI pointing to the HealthInterventions definition - instance: Inline HealthInterventions instance data
Value set for Health System Challenges (Classification of Digital Health System Categories v1, 2018). Includes all 25 system category codes (A–Y).

A professional involved in the administration and oversight of health systems.
Health system managers use DHIs to: - Manage health workforce information, performance, and certification (3.1) - Oversee supply chain, inventory, cold chain, and procurement (3.2) - Receive notifications of public health events (3.3) - Register and certify vital events — births and deaths (3.4) - Administer health coverage schemes, billing, payroll, and budgets (3.5) - Monitor and track health equipment and assets (3.6) - Manage health facility information and conduct assessments (3.7) - Manage person-centred health certificate information (3.8)
**ISCO-08**: 1342 (Health services managers), 2446 (Social work professionals n.e.c.), 3354 (Government social benefits officials), 4311 (Accounting and bookkeeping clerks).
**Examples**: District health officer, programme manager, supply chain officer, HMIS coordinator, hospital administrator, vital registration officer, health insurance administrator.

A member of the health workforce who delivers health interventions. This group has also been described as 'health workers' or 'healthcare workers'.
Healthcare providers use DHIs to: - Identify and register persons for health services (2.1) - Manage person-centred health records (2.2) - Receive clinical decision support prompts and checklists (2.3) - Conduct telemedicine consultations and remote monitoring (2.4) - Communicate with supervisors, peers, and receive AI-assisted content (2.5) - Coordinate referrals and emergency transport (2.6) - Schedule and plan their clinical activities (2.7) - Access training content and assessments (2.8) - Manage prescriptions and medication adherence (2.9) - Order and receive laboratory and diagnostic results (2.10) - Verify health coverage and receive payments from individuals (2.11)
**ISCO-08**: 2211 (Generalist medical practitioners), 2212 (Specialist medical practitioners), 2221 (Nursing professionals), 2222 (Midwifery professionals), 3211 (Medical imaging and therapeutic equipment technicians), 3212 (Medical and pathology laboratory technicians), 3213 (Pharmaceutical technicians and assistants), 3221 (Nursing associate professionals), 3222 (Midwifery associate professionals), 3255 (Community health workers).
**Examples**: Physician, nurse, midwife, clinical officer, pharmacist, laboratory technician, dentist, allied health professional.

name.value: Hierarchy of the Classification of Digital Health Interventions v2

description.value: Mapping to represent hierarchy within the Classification of Digital Interventions, Services and Applications in Health (CDISAH) v2.
ISCO-08 codes from the International Labour Organization official classification
Extensible value set of ISCO-08 codes for persona classification

A statement of how to put guidance into practice, printed in a publication whose publicationType is implementation-guidance or methodology: the handbook's "products that are not guidelines" (§1.9), a "how to" document that makes no recommendations of its own. Not a recommendation, and not a good practice statement — both are made by a guideline and approved by the GRC; this is neither. It carries no kind, direction, strength or certainty, because nothing graded it. A handbook's own "Best practices" lists are the typical source. Owner ruling 1b, 2026-10-12: model these as their own class, not as recommendation nodes of a new kind. statement is verbatim and is the only stored copy, as recommendation's is. identifier is used in the IRI. There is no remark: L1 3.0's remark is minted under a recommendation (its iriPattern) and hasRemark starts at one, so a remark of a practice needs L1 itself to change — proposed upstream, not patched here. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/implementation-practice.

A node in the ingested library L1 is read from: a source document, a section or a block, addressed by the library's own IRI. Opaque, as L1 asserts nothing about the library's internal model; the library is upstream, so pointing at it keeps the layering rule. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/library-node.
All codes of KGCertainty.

GRADE certainty of evidence. The 2014 handbook calls it quality of evidence and names certainty as a synonym (§9.1). Rated per outcome on evidence; the overall certainty on a recommendation is the lowest across its critical outcomes (§9.6). Source: smart-kg ontology/l1/l1.json valueSets "certainty"; WHO handbook for guideline development (2014) §9.1, §9.5–9.6.
All codes of KGChangeStatus.

Whether this edition of a consolidated guideline introduces, updates or carries a recommendation or indicator unchanged. Printed as NEW / UPDATE tags. Source: smart-kg ontology/l1/l1.json valueSets "change-status"; Consolidated guidelines on person-centred HIV strategic information (2022), summary recommendations; handbook §1.7.2.

One citation string exactly as written in a DAK artefact. A cell holding several citations yields several nodes. Content-addressed in the DAK's namespace, so one string is one node across artefacts. Where a citation was found is recorded by appearsIn (L2) and by each use edge (L2-DMN, L3 citesSource), not on the node. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/citation.
All codes of KGCitationKind.

Whether a citation string names a source, or stands in for one that is missing. Source: smart-kg ontology/l1/l1.json valueSets "citation-kind"; IMMZ DAK indicators workbook: '[Add appropriate reference]'.
All codes of KGL1Classes.
The classes of the L1 layer of the SMART Guidelines knowledge graph. A node's `type` is one of these. Source: smart-base/L1/schemas/L1.ts (migrated from smart-kg ontology/L1/L1.json).
All codes of KGElementType.
What kind of printed block a publication element is. Source: smart-kg ontology/l1/l1.json valueSets "element-type"; Observed in the ANC and HIV SI guidelines and the immunization summary tables.
One row of an evidence profile: the evidence for one outcome of one key question, with its certainty (handbook §9.2). Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/evidence.
All codes of KGEvidenceType.

Which kind of evidence a row is, and so which scale its certainty is on: GRADE for effects, GRADE-CERQual for qualitative findings. Source: smart-kg ontology/l1/l1.json valueSets "evidence-type"; ANC guideline (2016) methods (GRADE and GRADE-CERQual).
One L1 knowledge-graph document: typed nodes and reified edges, provenance-pinned to the sources it was extracted from. In JSON the context element is written @context.
All codes of KGGrcStatus.

Whether the Guideline Review Committee approved the publication. All WHO publications containing recommendations must be approved (handbook §1.10.1); a consolidated guideline whose recommendations were all previously approved and unchanged does not require review (§1.7.2). Absent means not recorded — not the same as not reviewed. Source: smart-kg ontology/l1/l1.json valueSets "grc-status"; WHO handbook for guideline development (2014), §1.7.2, §1.10.1.

An intervention identified in a WHO catalogue or classification (UHC Compendium, ICHI, CDHI), digital interventions included. A peer of recommendation, not a recommendation. A DAK may draw on both. Corresponds to HealthInterventions: identifier and description correspond to HealthInterventions.id and description[x]; not a Parent because HealthInterventions requires reference 1..* DublinCore, which here is an edge (definedIn) rather than a field. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/health-intervention.
All codes of KGIdentifierType.

Which kind of identifier a publication carries. The first available, in this order, builds the publication IRI. url comes last: a web address is the least stable identifier and is used only for sources that have no other. Source: smart-kg ontology/l1/l1.json valueSets "identifier-type"; WHO IRIS practice; CDHIv2.fsh carries an ISBN.

A WHO indicator, identified by its published reference number. Printed in several places (HIV SI 2022: summary list, Table 2.3, reference sheet) and stored once. variants is a list of {population, definition, numerator, denominator} for population-specific or level-specific forms (PRV.17, PRV.3). Corresponds to ProgramIndicator: definition, numerator, denominator and disaggregation are ProgramIndicator's elements and types (markdown); not a Parent because ProgramIndicator makes them 1..1 and an L1 indicator is recorded with what its source prints. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/indicator.
All codes of KGInterventionType.

DRAFT. What kind of intervention a recommendation or catalogued intervention concerns. To be aligned with the UHC Compendium's categories once checked. Source: smart-kg ontology/l1/l1.json valueSets "intervention-type"; WHO handbook §1.7.1 (clinical, health system, public health, diagnostic, surveillance); digital interventions per CDHI.

A question in PICO format, framed before the evidence search (handbook §7.1–7.4). P and C are verbatim text with codes through crossReferences; I is also joined to a catalogued intervention; O is the outcome node. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/key-question.

An outcome a guideline group chose to judge a key question by, with its importance in this guideline (handbook §7.6). A node because evidence attaches to it and one list is shared by several questions (ANC Web annex 1). Flat: one node per specific outcome. name as first printed; aliases are the other printed forms (e.g. 'EGWG'); category is the printed group heading (e.g. 'Fetal/newborn morbidity'). Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/outcome.
All codes of KGOutcomeImportance.

How the guideline development group rated an outcome on the 1–9 scale: 7–9 critical, 4–6 important. Unimportant outcomes are not carried into evidence profiles, so they have no code here. Source: smart-kg ontology/l1/l1.json valueSets "outcome-importance"; WHO handbook for guideline development (2014) §7.6, Fig. 7.1.
All codes of KGL1Predicates.

The predicates of the L1 layer. An edge's `predicate` is one of these; which (source, target) pairs each licenses is the layer's edge table. Source: smart-base/L1/schemas/L1.ts (migrated from smart-kg ontology/L1/L1.json).

A WHO publication: a guideline of any of the handbook's types, a position paper, a summary table, a classification, implementation guidance, or a supplement. Metadata follows Dublin Core. identifiers is a list of {type, value}; type is from identifier-type, and the first of isbn, iris-handle, doi, issn, url builds the IRI, so an edition change is a new publication. issued and modified are Dublin Core. reviewBy is the handbook's review-by date (§12.5.1). sha256 pins the PDF. Derives from DublinCore (smart-base input/fsh/models/DublinCore.fsh); title, creator, publisher, language, rights are its elements. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/publication.

One printed block: a table, a table row, a footnote, a figure, a chart, an image, a flowchart, a box or a list. It records where something is printed and exactly what is printed that no content node holds. It carries no meaning of its own; meaning lives in content nodes, joined by presentedIn. columns is the header text, verbatim. columnMap names, per column, the content field that fills it when the table is re-rendered (e.g. 'Recommendation' -> statement). cells holds only text no content node holds; a cell filled through columnMap is null. text is for unmodelled printed text such as a footnote that is not a remark. sha256 is for images. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/publication-element.
A chapter, annex or numbered section, at any depth. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/publication-section.
All codes of KGPublicationType.

What kind of publication this is. The distinction that matters most for provenance is guideline versus not: a summary table or position paper restates recommendations made elsewhere, and a §1.9 product makes none of its own. Conflating them makes a citation resolve to the wrong authority. Source: smart-kg ontology/l1/l1.json valueSets "publication-type"; WHO handbook for guideline development (2014), Table 1.2 and §1.7–1.9; the BCG decision table's citation for summary-table; CDHIv2.fsh for classification.

A normative statement from a WHO guideline. Kinds other than a graded recommendation (context-specific, research-only, good practice statement, no-recommendation) are the same node with a different kind. statement is verbatim and is the only stored copy. intervention, population, setting, provider and timing are verbatim slots taken from the statement, its remarks, or the enclosing caption or heading. setting absorbs the former conditionality. identifier is the published number (e.g. A.1.1), used in the IRI; sub-recommendations append their letter. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/recommendation.
All codes of KGRecommendationDirection.

For or against. The handbook prefers "we recommend against X" to "X is not recommended", which is ambiguous between against and no recommendation (§10.6). Source: smart-kg ontology/l1/l1.json valueSets "recommendation-direction"; WHO handbook for guideline development (2014) §10.1, §10.6.
All codes of KGRecommendationKind.

What sort of normative statement this is. Grading is optional: ANC 2016 prints a direction ('Recommended', 'Not recommended') and no GRADE strength. A strength always needs a direction. A good practice statement and a no-recommendation carry no strength or certainty, and a no-recommendation carries no direction. Source: smart-kg ontology/l1/l1.json valueSets "recommendation-kind"; WHO handbook §10.4, §10.7; ANC guideline (2016) Table 1, verified; Guyatt et al. 2016 on good practice statements.
All codes of KGRecommendationStatus.

Whether a recommendation is still in force. Recommendations in one guideline go out of date at different times (§1.7.2), and a department that doubts a recommendation's validity should say so before the update is done (§12.5.4). This is what impact analysis filters on. Source: smart-kg ontology/l1/l1.json valueSets "recommendation-status"; WHO handbook for guideline development (2014) §1.7.2, §12.5.
All codes of KGRecommendationStrength.

GRADE strength. Strength is not certainty: a strong recommendation can rest on low-certainty evidence and a conditional one on high. Record "weak" as conditional; the handbook treats them as synonyms (§10.4). Source: smart-kg ontology/l1/l1.json valueSets "recommendation-strength"; WHO handbook for guideline development (2014) §10.4.

One row of a DAK artefact's own reference list: '(1)' and the full bibliographic text and URL it stands for. Resolved once; every citation numbered to it shares the result. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/reference-entry.
A remark attached to a recommendation (handbook §10.6). May also be printed as a table footnote. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/remark.
All codes of KGRemarkType.

What a remark is for. Grounded in the six remarks attached to ANC recommendation A.1.1. Source: smart-kg ontology/l1/l1.json valueSets "remark-type"; ANC guideline (2016) p. 15; handbook §10.6, §10.8.
All codes of KGResolutionStatus.

Whether a citation string has been matched to what it cites. `ambiguous` is a legitimate terminal state — two publications with similar titles is a question for a person — and must not be collapsed to resolved. Source: smart-kg ontology/l1/l1.json valueSets "resolution-status"; docs/SCOPE.md.
All codes of KGRowType.
The role of a row within a table. Source: smart-kg ontology/l1/l1.json valueSets "row-type"; HIV SI guideline Table 2.3; ANC Table 1.

A code in an external terminology — ICD-10, ICD-11, SNOMED CT, ATC, or a WHO classification such as CDHI. CROSS-REFERENCE ONLY. It records system, code and display, and asserts NOTHING about the terminology: no hierarchy, no subsumption, no synonyms, no post-coordination. The terminology has its own authority, its own release cycle and its own tooling, and a partial copy here would be wrong within one release. Resolve meaning against the terminology server, not against this graph. Derives from Coding (FHIR R4 core datatype); system, code, display, version are its elements. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/terminology-code.
All codes of KGTerminologySystem.

Code systems a DAK is expected to use. An unknown system is a warning, because a misspelt system silently breaks joins across guidelines. Source: smart-kg ontology/l1/l1.json valueSets "terminology-system"; smart-base input/fsh/profiles/SGLogicalModel.fsh and Aliases.fsh; UHC Compendium; CDHIv2.fsh.
All codes of KGL1LibraryClasses.

The classes of the L1Library layer of the SMART Guidelines knowledge graph. A node's `type` is one of these. Source: smart-base/L1/schemas/l1-library.ts (migrated from smart-kg ontology/l1-library/l1-library.json).
All codes of KGL1LibraryPredicates.

The predicates of the L1Library layer. An edge's `predicate` is one of these; which (source, target) pairs each licenses is the layer's edge table. Source: smart-base/L1/schemas/l1-library.ts (migrated from smart-kg ontology/l1-library/l1-library.json).

A start, end or intermediate event (WHO's DAK BPMN draw intermediate throw and catch events inside sub-processes). Same connectivity argument as gateway, plus one of its own: entry and exit points are what make 'is this task reachable' and 'does this path terminate' answerable at all. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/bpmn-event.

One BPMN file as a unit -- the `bpmn:definitions` root. Shares its IRI with the l1:external-artifact for the same file, so the component that points at it and the subgraph that opens it name one resource. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/bpmn-definitions.

A branch or merge. Included for connectivity rather than for a cross-model edge: a flow through a gateway with no node would point at nothing, and every reachability question over the process would break at the first decision point. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/bpmn-gateway.

A pool: a role that owns part of the collaboration. The lifecycle BPMN has 8 and declares no laneSet at all, so the pool is the only unit of role assignment present and its @name is the sole link to a persona. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/bpmn-participant.

One `bpmn:process`. Present as a node because a participant references it by processRef, and without it the pool-to-element attribution has nothing to travel through. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/bpmn-process.

A task or sub-process. It is what a DMN usingTask href points at, what sequence flows connect, and what a DAK-level task entry describes. Sub-processes carry isSubProcess rather than getting a class of their own -- the lifecycle BPMN has exactly one. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/bpmn-task.
All codes of KGGatewayDirection.

BPMN 2.0's gatewayDirection. Added by the smart-base migration: smart-kg named the property without binding it. Source: smart-kg ontology/l2-bpmn/l2-bpmn.json valueSets "gateway-direction"; OMG BPMN 2.0.2, Gateway.gatewayDirection.

A `dmn:decision` -- the question being answered, and the node that carries the link back to the BPMN task invoking it. A file may hold several; the BCG file holds one. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/dmn-decision.

name.value: Knowledge graph L2-DMN: DMN Decision Table

description.value: The table realising a decision. Separate from dmn-decision because DMN permits other expression kinds -- a literal expression, an invocation -- and collapsing the two would make the graph unable to say which was used. hitPolicy is optional and recorded as null when absent, which it is in the BCG table. DMN's default is UNIQUE, but asserting it here would put words in the author's mouth. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/dmn-decision-table.

name.value: Knowledge graph L2-DMN: dmn entry kind

description.value: All codes of KGDmnEntryKind.

name.value: Knowledge graph L2-DMN: dmn entry kind

description.value: Which DMN element type a column's cells are serialised as. Added by the smart-base migration from smart-kg's propertyNote, which named the two values in prose. Source: smart-kg ontology/l2-dmn/l2-dmn.json valueSets "dmn-entry-kind"; OMG DMN 1.3, DecisionRule.outputEntry and annotationEntry.

One DMN file as a unit -- the `dmn:definitions` root. Shares its IRI with the l1:external-artifact for the same file, so the l2:decision-support-logic component that points at it and this subgraph name one resource. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/dmn-definitions.

name.value: Knowledge graph L2-DMN: DMN Input Clause

description.value: An input column. Its expression text is where data element names are embedded, which is the only reason this is a node rather than a property of the table. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/dmn-input-clause.

name.value: Knowledge graph L2-DMN: DMN Output Clause

description.value: An output column. The BCG table's four are Care Plan, Guidance displayed to health worker, Annotations and Reference(s). These are column DEFINITIONS in a decision table, not clinical records: no edge from this class reaches an execution artefact, and none may. serialisedAs is outputEntry or annotationEntry -- DMN splits the columns across two element types and the split is positional, so recording it is what lets a rule's cells be matched back to their columns. isReferenceColumn marks the L1 column, found by its description rather than its index. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/dmn-output-clause.

One row. Its input and output cells are carried as properties, not nodes: 250 of them in the BCG table alone, none the target of a cross-model edge. What the rule needs a node for is its citation edge into L1. conditions and outputs are arrays of {clause, description, text}. DMN puts the formal expression in description and the human-readable gloss in text, and both are worth keeping -- the gloss is what a reviewer reads and the expression is what an implementer builds. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/dmn-rule.
All codes of KGArtifactKind.

What kind of file an external artefact is. Moved with the class from L1, where it was free text. Source: smart-kg ontology/l2/l2.json valueSets "artifact-kind"; Files observed in smart-base and in WHO's immunizations DAK (canonical http://smart.who.int/immunizations).

name.value: Knowledge graph L2: Business Process Workflow

description.value: DAK component 4. NOT the BPMN file -- the component that points at one. `source 1..1 uri` is that pointer, and the BPMN's interior is the l2-bpmn subgraph, reached through the external-artifact this sourcedFrom targets. `objectives 1..1 markdown` is required by BusinessProcessWorkflow.fsh and has no counterpart anywhere in BPMN XML, so it can only ever come from the FSH instance. resolutionStatus is `unresolved` on a component that something else names but no DAK declares -- an L3 artefact whose title carries the component id, for instance. The node exists so the gap is queryable and carries the referenced id and nothing else. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/business-process.
All codes of KGL2Classes.
The classes of the L2 layer of the SMART Guidelines knowledge graph. A node's `type` is one of these. Source: smart-base/L1/schemas/L2.ts (migrated from smart-kg ontology/L2/L2.json).
All codes of KGConformanceExpectation.

The conformance verb of a requirement statement. Added by the smart-base migration from smart-kg's propertyNote, which named the four values in prose. Source: smart-kg ontology/l2/l2.json valueSets "conformance-expectation"; http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/conformance-expectation.

name.value: Knowledge graph L2: Core Data Element

description.value: DAK component 5. CoreDataElement.fsh calls itself "the ONE EXCEPTION to allowing FHIR R4 models into the DAK LMs": `type` is one of valueset | codesystem | conceptmap | logicalmodel and `canonical 1..1 uri` points at it. The canonical is recorded; nothing inside it is copied, because FHIR is its own query layer. `name`, `resolutionStatus` and `extractionRule` are for elements recovered from DMN input expressions rather than declared in a dictionary. A recovered element is a name that was REFERENCED, not a definition that was found, and only a resolved one may carry a canonical. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/data-element.

DAK component 6. The whole model is an id, an optional description and `source 1..1 uri` to a DMN file. Nothing about the decision itself -- which is the gap the l2-dmn subgraph fills. resolutionStatus is `unresolved` on a component that something else names but no DAK declares -- an L3 artefact whose title carries the component id, for instance. The node exists so the gap is queryable and carries the referenced id and nothing else. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/decision-support-logic.

name.value: Knowledge graph L2: Digital Adaptation Kit

description.value: The kit itself. Properties are exactly the metadata fields DAK.fsh declares and dak.json carries -- no more, so that a dak node can be produced from a real file without anything being invented. canonicalUrl equals publicationUrl on a release branch and previewUrl on a development branch, per DAK.fsh. Both are kept because which one canonicalUrl currently equals is what says whether a graph describes a release or a build. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/dak.

A DAK file addressed by canonical URL: a BPMN process, a DMN decision table, a FHIR resource, a workbook. Deliberately opaque: it carries an IRI and a kind, and nothing about its interior. The L2-BPMN, L2-DMN and L3 classes that describe a file's interior elaborate this class at the same IRI. Moved here from L1 in 3.0 unchanged: a DAK file is the DAK's material, not WHO content. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/external-artifact.

DAK component 8, first half. The as-a/I-want/so-that shape: `activity`, `capability[x]`, `benefit[x]`, and `actor 0..* Reference(SGActor)`. The 41 committed instances use the R5 SGRequirements profile rather than this logical model, so a real instance carries `statement` entries and a userstory extension; both shapes are accommodated and `profile` records which was read. resolutionStatus is `unresolved` on a component that something else names but no DAK declares -- an L3 artefact whose title carries the component id, for instance. The node exists so the gap is queryable and carries the referenced id and nothing else. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/functional-requirement.

DAK component 2. Grounded in GenericPersona.fsh -- title, id, description, otherNames, iscoCode bound to ISCO08ValueSet -- and in the 22 committed ActorDefinition instances that carry name, title, type and description. The two disagree about where ISCO lives, which the properties record rather than smooth over. `title` is the human-readable label a BPMN pool matches on; `name` is the CamelCase identifier a Canonical() reference matches on. They are different strings for the same persona and conflating them is precisely how the pool join breaks. GenericPersona.fsh declares `iscoCode 0..* code`, but the committed ActorDefinitions record ISCO in prose inside description, so iscoCode is usually empty and is not authoritative. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/persona.

DAK component 8, second half. `requirement 1..1 markdown`, an optional category and classification codings. Kept separate from the functional half because the fields genuinely differ -- a non-functional requirement has no actor and no benefit. resolutionStatus is `unresolved` on a component that something else names but no DAK declares -- an L3 artefact whose title carries the component id, for instance. The node exists so the gap is queryable and carries the referenced id and nothing else. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/non-functional-requirement.
All codes of KGL2Predicates.

The predicates of the L2 layer. An edge's `predicate` is one of these; which (source, target) pairs each licenses is the layer's edge table. Source: smart-base/L1/schemas/L2.ts (migrated from smart-kg ontology/L2/L2.json).

DAK component 7. Named program-indicator and not `indicator` because L1 already declares an `indicator` -- one normatively defined in a publication. They are different things: this is the DAK's operational measure, and `derivedFrom` is how it points at the normative one. Collapsing them would silently merge a WHO definition with a country's implementation of it. numerator, denominator and disaggregation are all `1..1 markdown` -- prose, not a computable expression. Nothing here should be read as a calculable measure; the L3 FHIR Measure is where that would live. resolutionStatus is `unresolved` on a component that something else names but no DAK declares -- an L3 artefact whose title carries the component id, for instance. The node exists so the gap is queryable and carries the referenced id and nothing else. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/program-indicator.
All codes of KGPublicationStatus.

FHIR PublicationStatus, which DAK.fsh's status and every L3 resource's status take. Added by the smart-base migration: smart-kg named these properties without binding them. Source: smart-kg ontology/l2/l2.json valueSets "publication-status"; http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/publication-status.

One numbered, labelled statement inside a requirement, with a conformance verb. A node rather than a property because conformance is queried across a whole DAK -- 'every SHALL in this kit, and what fulfils it' is the question requirements exist to answer. It also carries its own success criteria, so 'what would show this SHALL is met' is answerable per statement rather than per requirement. conformance is the FHIR ConformanceExpectation verb: SHALL, SHOULD, MAY or SHOULD-NOT. Across the 41 committed instances it is 155 SHALL and 15 SHOULD. successCriteria is a LIST of objects, each {key, criterion, verification}: `key` is unique within the statement (e.g. SC-1), `criterion` is a checkable sentence, and `verification` is one of test | inspection | review | analysis -- the same field name and enum as folio-assistant's requirement.ts `successCriteria`, so the two map 1:1. smart-base types it, so the shape is enforced by the schema; a statement with no successCriteria is still valid (the 170 statements committed in smart-base carry none). Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/requirement-statement.

When an intervention is due, as a DAK component. NOT declared by DAK.fsh -- it is added here because the published SOP lists Scheduling Logic as an active L2 input (spreadsheets under input/scheduling-logic), WHO's ArchiMate model declares it a BusinessObject realised by PlanDefinition, and L1's schedules needed an L2 component to reach (since L1 3.0, a recommendation's timing slot). Note that the SOP's own L3 row for scheduling is present but HTML-commented-out and there is no l3_schedulinglogic.md page, so WHO has drafted the mapping and not activated it; the L3 edge is licensed here as a deliberate departure, recorded rather than hidden. resolutionStatus is `unresolved` on a component that something else names but no DAK declares -- an L3 artefact whose title carries the component id, for instance. The node exists so the gap is queryable and carries the referenced id and nothing else. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/scheduling-logic.

One task of a DAK business process, as the DAK document's "notes and annotations" describe it: identifier, name, description, and the personas, data elements, requirements and decision tables it links to. A node rather than a property because the same task is also drawn in the BPMN file, and the two have to be joinable to be checkable against each other (`describes`). Read from a BPMN file's `dak-task-annotations/v1` sidecar (smart-base/L2-bpmn/schemas/task-annotations.ts); BusinessProcessWorkflow's `task 0..*` backbone carries the first three fields of the same thing. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/dak-task.

DAK component 9. `feature 1..1 uri` to a Gherkin feature file, plus an optional description. The feature file's interior is not modelled: no DAK in this estate ships one yet, so a subgraph for it would have no instance to check it against. resolutionStatus is `unresolved` on a component that something else names but no DAK declares -- an L3 artefact whose title carries the component id, for instance. The node exists so the gap is queryable and carries the referenced id and nothing else. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/test-scenario.

DAK component 3. A narrative describing how personas interact. Carries `personas 0..* id`, which is the only structured link between the narrative layer and the personas it names. resolutionStatus is `unresolved` on a component that something else names but no DAK declares -- an L3 artefact whose title carries the component id, for instance. The node exists so the gap is queryable and carries the referenced id and nothing else. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/user-scenario.
All codes of KGVerificationMethod.

How a success criterion is verified: the classic verification methods, the same field name and codes as folio-assistant's requirement.ts `successCriteria`, so the two map 1:1. From litlfred/smart-kg main (folio-assistant#2406). Source: smart-kg ontology/l2/l2.json valueSets "verification-method"; folio-assistant-core schemas requirement.ts successCriteria.verification.
All codes of KGL2BPMNClasses.

The classes of the L2BPMN layer of the SMART Guidelines knowledge graph. A node's `type` is one of these. Source: smart-base/L1/schemas/L2-BPMN.ts (migrated from smart-kg ontology/L2-BPMN/L2-BPMN.json).
All codes of KGL2BPMNPredicates.

The predicates of the L2BPMN layer. An edge's `predicate` is one of these; which (source, target) pairs each licenses is the layer's edge table. Source: smart-base/L1/schemas/L2-BPMN.ts (migrated from smart-kg ontology/L2-BPMN/L2-BPMN.json).
All codes of KGL2DMNClasses.
The classes of the L2DMN layer of the SMART Guidelines knowledge graph. A node's `type` is one of these. Source: smart-base/L1/schemas/L2-DMN.ts (migrated from smart-kg ontology/L2-DMN/L2-DMN.json).
All codes of KGL2DMNPredicates.

The predicates of the L2DMN layer. An edge's `predicate` is one of these; which (source, target) pairs each licenses is the layer's edge table. Source: smart-base/L1/schemas/L2-DMN.ts (migrated from smart-kg ontology/L2-DMN/L2-DMN.json).

A FHIR ActivityDefinition -- the concrete act a plan's action invokes. Reached from a PlanDefinition action's `definitionCanonical`, which is a real reference rather than a convention. 3 in the immunizations IG: two cpg-immunizationactivity, one cpg-communicationactivity. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/activity-definition.

A FHIR ActorDefinition -- an L2 persona made a FHIR resource. ZERO in the immunizations IG and 22 in smart-base, which is itself worth a coverage query. The SOP names no profile for it and says one is not currently possible because SUSHI cannot profile an R5 resource in an R4 IG, and it tells authors not to assign an identifier -- so expect a bare resource and do not infer more. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/actor-definition.
All codes of KGL3Classes.
The classes of the L3 layer of the SMART Guidelines knowledge graph. A node's `type` is one of these. Source: smart-base/L1/schemas/L3.ts (migrated from smart-kg ontology/L3/L3.json).

A FHIR CodeSystem. The SOP says each guideline defines one guideline-level code system holding a concept for every data dictionary element -- which is what makes `code[WHO] = IMMZ.DE9` on a logical model element resolvable. 6 in the immunizations IG. The codes themselves are not copied here. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/code-system.

A FHIR ConceptMap -- one per target code system in the dictionary's terminology mappings. 8 in the immunizations IG. Records that a mapping exists; the mappings themselves belong to terminology. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/concept-map.

A .cql file on disk, as opposed to the FHIR Library resource that wraps it. A node so that the mapping table's four CQL rows -- CQL Concepts and CQL Data Elements under Elements, CQL under Decision Tables, CQL IndicatorLogic under Indicators -- do not dead-end. It carries a name, a path and a hash and NOTHING about the logic: no expressions, no comment tags, no data requirements. 279 in the immunizations IG. The l3-cql subgraph is where that content belongs, and it is not built yet. No canonical, because a .cql file is not a FHIR resource and has no canonical URL. It is reached through the Library that wraps it. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/cql-library.

A FHIR Library -- the resource that carries CQL. Indexed by canonical and status only. Its CONTENTS are deliberately out of scope: a future l3-cql subgraph will elaborate this same IRI, exactly as l2-bpmn elaborates a BPMN file. 279 in the immunizations IG, joined to their PlanDefinition by the `{id}Logic` suffix. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/library.

A StructureDefinition with kind `logical` -- one data dictionary tab as a data structure. Distinct from `profile`, which constrains a FHIR resource: WHO's ArchiMate model has Logical Model realising Data Object while Profile realises Data Element, and the two are not interchangeable. 15 in the immunizations IG. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/structure-definition.

A FHIR Measure -- an indicator made computable. 41 in the immunizations IG, all declaring proportion-measure-cqfm; the SOP makes the profile depend on scoring type, which is why the profile is read rather than assumed. Joined to its L2 indicator by id convention (IMMZ.IND.08 -> IMMZIND08). Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/measure.

A FHIR PlanDefinition. The published mapping gives it two sources -- Processes and Decision Tables -- so a PlanDefinition alone does not say which it came from; the implementedBy edge does. 138 in the immunizations IG, all declaring cpg-recommendationdefinition, all decision tables. Shares its IRI with the l1:external-artifact for the same canonical. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/plan-definition.
All codes of KGL3Predicates.

The predicates of the L3 layer. An edge's `predicate` is one of these; which (source, target) pairs each licenses is the layer's edge table. Source: smart-base/L1/schemas/L3.ts (migrated from smart-kg ontology/L3/L3.json).

A StructureDefinition constraining a FHIR resource. Separate from structure-definition for the reason above. 5 in the immunizations IG. Its internals -- differentials, element definitions, bindings -- are the clearest case of what this layer refuses to re-represent. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/profile.

A FHIR Questionnaire -- a data-collection form over a logical model. 10 in the immunizations IG. Its `sdc-questionnaire-targetStructureMap` extension names the StructureMap that extracts it, which is a real canonical reference. The SOP states no linkId convention and none exists in the estate, so no edge is licensed on linkId. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/questionnaire.

A FHIR Requirements resource. The ONE place the published SOP names an SG profile -- SGRequirements -- and the grain is one resource per business process holding many statements, not one per requirement. ZERO in the immunizations IG and 41 in smart-base. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/requirements.

name.value: Knowledge graph L3: structure definition kind

description.value: FHIR StructureDefinitionKind. Added by the smart-base migration: smart-kg named the property without binding it. Source: smart-kg ontology/l3/l3.json valueSets "structure-definition-kind"; http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/structure-definition-kind.

A FHIR StructureMap. The SOP requires them in threes -- QuestionnaireResponse to logical model, logical model to resource, and a grouping map -- so a count that is not a multiple of three is worth a look. 16 .fml files in the immunizations IG. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/structure-map.

A FHIR ValueSet. 192 in the immunizations IG -- the most numerous artefact of all. Indexed by canonical; its expansion, its compose rules and the codes it contains are terminology, which docs/SCOPE.md keeps at arm's length as firmly here as at L1. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/value-set.
All codes of KGDerivation.

How a node or edge of a SMART Guidelines knowledge graph came to be. Every node and edge is exactly one of the three, and `decided` is the one a reviewer needs to find. Source: smart-kg shapes/recommendation-graph.schema.json $defs.derivation.
One reified statement: a predicate from a source node to a target node, with its derivation and evidence.
Where a node or edge came from in its source. Required on anything not mechanically derived.
One typed node of a knowledge-graph document. Its instance fields are an instance of the logical model of its class (see definedBy), e.g. KGPublication for a publication.
A source a graph document was extracted from, pinned by hash.

name.value: Mapping from CDHI v1 to CDISAH v2

description.value:
Mapping from the Classification of Digital Health Interventions v1 (CDHI v1, 2018) to the Classification of Digital Interventions, Services and Applications in Health v2 (CDISAH v2, 2023).
Key structural changes reflected in this map: - User group labels updated throughout (e.g. 'Clients' → 'Persons', 'Health workers' → 'Healthcare providers', 'Health system managers' → 'Health management and support personnel'). - Civil Registration and Vital Statistics (CRVS) consolidated: six v1 codes (3.4.1–3.4.6) merged into two v2 codes (3.4.1, 3.4.2). - Health financing section restructured: v1 3.5.1 (insurance membership) and 3.5.2 (billing) updated; v1 3.5.3–3.5.6 shifted by one (now 3.5.4–3.5.6 + new 3.5.3). - Data services (group 4) substantially revised: 4.1.1 changed scope, 4.3 expanded from 4 to 5 codes, 4.4 split from 1 to 3 codes, 4.5 is entirely new. - New v2 categories with no v1 equivalent are listed as 'unmatched' targets.

name.value: Mapping from CDSC v1 to Services and Application Types v2

description.value:
Mapping from the Classification of Digital Health System Categories v1 (CDSCv1, 2018) to the Classification of Digital Health Services and Application Types v2 (CDSCv2, 2023).
The v1 used 25 single-letter codes (A–Y). The v2 completely restructured this into 5 representations within the digital health enterprise architecture, each with alphanumeric codes (A1–A9, B1–B8, C1–C11, D1–D8, E1–E2).
Several new v2 categories have no v1 equivalent: A3 (Decision support), A4 (Diagnostics), B1 (Blood bank), B3 (Health program monitoring), B7 (Patient administration), C4 (Facility registries), C5 (Health worker registry), C7 (Immunisation information), C8 (Master patient index), C9 (Product catalogues), C10 (Public Key directories), D1 (Analytics), D3 (Data warehouses).

A member of the public who is a potential or current user of health services, including health prevention and wellness activities. Other terms used for this group include 'patient', 'client', 'individual', and 'health service user'. Caregivers of individuals receiving health services are also included.
Persons interact with DHIs to: - Receive targeted (1.1) and untargeted (1.2) health communications - Communicate with other persons as peers (1.3) - Track their own health data and records (1.4) - Report health events and system feedback (1.5) - Access health information on demand including via chatbot/AI (1.6) - Manage their financial transactions related to health services (1.7) - Manage their consent for health data access and sharing (1.8)
**ISCO-08**: Not applicable (non-occupational role).
**Examples**: Patient, pregnant woman, caregiver, child, community member, health scheme beneficiary, person living with a chronic condition.

A programme manager responsible for the overall coordination and management of the Digital Adaptation Kit (DAK) development process. Programme managers lead scoping, resource allocation, timeline planning, and stakeholder engagement.
The DAK development team should be small (<10 people) and nimble. The Programme Manager ensures the team is empowered to self-organize and manage DAK-related work including collaboration with stakeholders, content development, validation, and publication.
Key activities: - Define DAK scope and purpose - Form and coordinate the DAK development team - Establish development process and governance - Define RASCI matrix for roles and responsibilities - Plan sprint iterations and maintain the DAK backlog - Coordinate SME consultations (workshops, country visits) - Draft project roadmap with milestone dates - Assess and secure resources and budget
**Source**: IG Starter Kit, L2 DAK Authoring, Section 1 "Plan"

A quality assurance specialist responsible for reviewing SMART Guidelines Implementation Guides for publication readiness. QC Reviewers use the publication checklist across L1-L4 layers, interpret QA validation reports, and verify artifact conformance and cross-component consistency.

A health area technical officer who coordinates the work on the DAK and performs first-pass review and validation of DAK content. Technical officers are part of the DAK development team and serve as the primary bridge between the development team and the broader group of Subject Matter Experts.
Key activities: - Coordinate DAK development work within the health programme area - Perform first-pass review of drafted DAK components - Validate that components accurately reflect L1 recommendations - Identify gaps, ambiguities, and alternatives in DAK content - Prepare agendas and questions for SME consultation meetings - Ensure content is software-neutral and context-appropriate - Spread awareness of SMART Guidelines within the department
**Source**: IG Starter Kit, L2 DAK Authoring, Section 2.2 "Validate DAK content with SMEs"

A specialist responsible for ensuring semantic interoperability of SMART Guidelines through proper terminology management. Terminologists manage the WHO Commons dictionary, concept mappings, and ensure every data element is mapped to approved standard terminologies.
Key activities: - Map data elements to WHO Commons dictionary concepts - Create and maintain CodeSystem resources - Create and maintain ValueSet resources - Create ConceptMap resources for cross-terminology mappings - Map to ICD-11, SNOMED CT, LOINC, IPS, and WHO FIC - Onboard new concepts into the Commons dictionary - Verify no duplicate or overlapping concept definitions - Review terminology bindings in logical models and profiles - Flag unapproved concepts as QA issues before publication
**Source**: IG Starter Kit, Governance Concepts page; L3 authoring pages for CodeSystems, ValueSets, ConceptMaps
